title: DFS: pre / in / post

hook.scenario: You have a 3-line recursive tree function: call left, call right, process node. Simply changing the position of that 1 processing line changes the entire purpose of the algorithm.
hook.question: Why does moving a single line of code turn tree cloning into tree deletion or sorted sorting?

why_it_exists.problem: Different tree tasks require different information availability. Cloning requires knowing parent values first; deleting or computing tree height requires knowing child results first.
why_it_exists.naive_solution: Using a single generic traversal and re-traversing the tree multiple times to gather parent or child data.
why_it_exists.better_idea: Select the exact DFS order (pre-order, in-order, or post-order) suited for your data dependency: process parents before children (pre), process between children (in), or process children before parents (post).

mental_model.intuition: The three DFS orders are identical recursive journeys; they only differ by when you record the node on your itinerary.
mental_model.description: Every DFS traversal traverses the exact same edges in the exact same sequence. Pre-order records a node on first entry (top-down), in-order records it after returning from the left child (left-to-right), and post-order records it after returning from both children (bottom-up).
mental_model.repeated_decision: do I record this node BEFORE, BETWEEN, or AFTER its two recursive calls?

explanation:
All three Depth-First Search orders execute the exact same recursive structural walk:
1. Recurse Left
2. Recurse Right

The ONLY difference is where the node 'visit' (processing or recording) happens relative to those two calls.

Code Comparison:
- Pre-order:
  visit(node)
  dfs(node.left)
  dfs(node.right)
- In-order:
  dfs(node.left)
  visit(node)
  dfs(node.right)
- Post-order:
  dfs(node.left)
  dfs(node.right)
  visit(node)

The Headline Payoffs:
1. Pre-Order (Top-Down): Useful for cloning or serializing trees. You process the parent before creating or copying its subtrees.
2. In-Order (Sorted Sequence): For a Binary Search Tree (BST), in-order traversal visits values in strictly non-decreasing sorted order.
3. Post-Order (Bottom-Up): Useful for subtree computations (height, diameter, subtree size) and directory deletion (`rm -rf`). You must process and free both child subtrees before you can safely process or delete the parent.

Concrete Walkthrough on BST:
Root `4` with left child `2` (which has left `1`, right `3`) and right child `5`.
Structure:
    4
   / \
  2   5
 / \
1   3

- Pre-order trace: `4` -> `2` -> `1` -> `3` -> `5`. (Top-down structure preserved).
- In-order trace: `1` -> `2` -> `3` -> `4` -> `5`. (Produces perfectly sorted sequence `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`).
- Post-order trace: `1` -> `3` -> `2` -> `5` -> `4`. (Leaves processed first, root processed absolute last).

key_points.title: Same Walk, Different Timing
key_points.detail: Pre-order visits on entry, in-order visits between children, post-order visits on exit.

key_points.title: BST In-Order Invariant
key_points.detail: In-order traversal of a valid BST ALWAYS yields elements in sorted ascending order.

key_points.title: Post-Order Bottom-Up Invariant
key_points.detail: Post-order guarantees child results are completely calculated before parent logic runs.

common_mistakes.title: Assuming in-order sorts any binary tree
common_mistakes.explanation: In-order traversal ONLY produces a sorted sequence if the binary tree satisfies the Binary Search Tree (BST) property.

common_mistakes.title: Believing pre, in, and post-order visit different nodes
common_mistakes.explanation: They visit the exact same set of nodes and traverse the exact same edges. Only the timing of when the node's action occurs changes.

common_mistakes.title: Using pre-order when child values are required
common_mistakes.explanation: Attempting to calculate subtree properties (like tree height) with pre-order leads to repetitive, inefficient top-down re-calculations.

when_not_to_use.scenario: Finding shortest path in unweighted tree level by level
when_not_to_use.reason: DFS explores deep paths to leaves first. Use BFS (level-order) to find shallowest target nodes efficiently.

failure_signals: You need to delete a file directory where subfolders must be emptied before parent folder removal.
You need to extract sorted elements from a BST.
You need to serialize a tree into a format that can recreate its exact structure.

engineering_examples.title: Recursive Directory Deletion (`rm -rf`)
engineering_examples.problem: Delete an entire directory tree from disk without leaving orphaned file handles.
engineering_examples.why_this_algorithm: Post-order traversal ensures all files and subdirectories inside a directory are deleted before removing the parent directory itself.

engineering_examples.title: Tree Serialization & Deserialization
engineering_examples.problem: Convert a binary tree structure into a string to send over a network.
engineering_examples.why_this_algorithm: Pre-order traversal records the root first followed by subtrees, allowing easy top-down reconstruction during deserialization.

recall_questions.q: What order does an in-order traversal of a Binary Search Tree produce?
recall_questions.answer: It produces a strictly ascending sorted sequence of the tree's values.

recall_questions.q: Why is post-order traversal used for directory deletion (`rm -rf`)?
recall_questions.answer: Because post-order processes all children before the parent node, ensuring subdirectories are emptied before deleting the parent folder.

recall_questions.q: What is the key difference between pre-order and post-order traversal?
recall_questions.answer: Pre-order processes the current node before visiting its subtrees (top-down), while post-order processes the current node after visiting its subtrees (bottom-up).

oa_questions.question: Find the k-th smallest element in a Binary Search Tree.
oa_questions.answer: Perform an in-order traversal (which visits BST nodes in sorted order) and return the k-th visited node.
oa_questions.approach: In-order DFS traversal yields sorted order; count visits up to k.

oa_questions.question: Serialize and deserialize a binary tree.
oa_questions.answer: Use pre-order traversal with null indicators to serialize. Reconstruct top-down using the pre-order string.
oa_questions.approach: Pre-order DFS encodes root before subtrees, allowing unambiguous reconstruction.

interesting_facts: Post-order traversal is also known as Reverse Polish Notation evaluation when applied to expression trees.
